text: Objects can have two kinds of attributes, and knowing the difference prevents a lot of confusion.
A class attribute, defined right in the class body, is shared by every single instance.
Here team equals Red belongs to the whole Player class at once.
[chuckle] Instance attributes, set inside init using self, are unique to each object.
So every player gets their own name and their own score, but they all share the same team.
[sniff] Change the class attribute on the class itself, and the update ripples out to everyone.
Suddenly both Alice and Bob are on the Blue team, because they shared that value.
[sigh] But if you set the attribute on one instance, that object gets its own private copy, overriding the shared one.
[groan] Use class attributes for shared constants, and instance attributes for the data that makes each object unique.
